name: Revelation First field census
schema_note: The fleet census core (slug, name, aka, url, operator, kind, unit, count, lifecycle, version_and_time, negative_tags, evidence, relations, unchecked, sources), after Labor Vector's labor census, extended for the field around the Revelation First thesis: intersections (one or more of four), evidence_kind, text_object (which texts), method, coverage, findings, stated_limits, answers and does_not_answer (which questions of composition, dating and machine reading this kind of evidence can and cannot settle), and rf_intersection (where it meets the Revelation First workstreams: the archive's reading, kept apart from the resource's own terms). Every quote is verbatim from a saved source.
organizing_question: What evidence does each resource hold on when and from what the New Testament writings were composed, and how do machines now read those texts?
correction: Revelation First ≠ Revelation Early. The pre-70 date is the old argument (Robinson, 1976; Gentry, 1989); Revelation First is the priority thesis: the rest of the New Testament unfolds from the Apocalypse.
